## The Compliance Gap Is Wider Than You Think

Most local governments have hundreds of untagged PDFs on their websites. The federal deadline is approaching fast.

### DOJ Enforcement Is Real

The Department of Justice finalized ADA Title II digital accessibility rules in April 2024. Compliance deadlines are April 24, 2026 for populations of 50,000+ and April 26, 2027 for smaller municipalities.

### Compliance Is More Than PDFs

ADA Title II requires WCAG 2.1 AA compliance for all web content — web pages, PDFs, videos, audio, and documents. Most governments are only thinking about PDFs when the rule covers everything on their website.

### No Single Tool Covers It All

Governments are cobbling together WCAG scanners, PDF remediators, and spreadsheets. Without a unified system, there's no defensible audit trail and no way to prove compliance to the DOJ.

ADA Title II Website Accessibility for Municipalities — Munibit

# A Website Platform Built to Support Accessibility

The DOJ requires small local governments to meet WCAG 2.1 Level AA web accessibility standards by April 26, 2028. Munibit's platform is built to support those requirements from day one, so every page, every form, and every document is supported.

Federal ADA Title II deadline for local governments under 50,000: April 26, 2028.

## What the DOJ's ADA Title II Rule Requires from Your Municipality.

The Department of Justice has finalized a rule under ADA Title II requiring local governments to meet WCAG 2.1 Level AA web accessibility standards. For governments under 50,000 population, the deadline is April 26, 2028.

#### Required Standard: WCAG 2.1 Level AA

WCAG 2.1 Level AA is the benchmark the DOJ requires. It covers how pages are structured, how forms work, how documents are displayed, and whether assistive technology like screen readers can navigate your site.

#### Deadline: April 26, 2028

Local governments with a population under 50,000 must meet the standard by April 26, 2028. There is no extension on record. The time to plan is now, not the week before the deadline.

#### It Is More Than Just Web Pages

The rule covers your full online presence, including online forms residents fill out, PDFs in your document library, and meeting minutes. A partially accessible site still carries risk.
